challenge.method: Extracted the README notice from the copyright through the period ending restriction 2. Stripped leading TeX comment markers and compared the result with the standalone text and decoded JSON licenseText. Recomputed ordered lowercase ASCII alphanumeric tokens, repeated the comparison with letters only and with case and punctuation preserved, and checked the annotated tag name and commit target against both raw URL pins.
challenge.results: All three ordered alphanumeric sequences have 81 tokens and the same SHA-256, 3e63c435490a00ba47443c9a1ff0802edfb8bb0174e4da36ad628218da36b838, when joined with single spaces. Letters-only tokenization gives 77 words in each source. The four numeric tokens are the two copyright years and two restriction numbers. The passages also match with case and punctuation preserved after comment removal and whitespace normalization. The standalone text equals decoded licenseText byte for byte. The annotated tag is v3.29.0 and targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, matching both data URLs.

limitations: The 81 count uses alphanumeric tokens and includes four numeric tokens. A letters-only count yields 77. The candidate's use of “words” depends on that tokenizer definition.
The SPDX text and detail share the same repository and revision and provide two representations of one authority. The tag binding rests on the repository API's unsigned annotated object.
The match covers the captured README notice and SPDX 3.29.0 only. Other versions, the macro implementation, the package catalog, installation, reuse, and legal effect require separate evidence.
reasoning: The bounded text agrees across all three representations, including under a comparison that preserves case and punctuation. The stated 81 count is reproducible with alphanumeric tokenization. The annotated release tag names the exact commit used by both SPDX representations.
